title: Henderson's band at the top; Whiteman's praise; strict inspections
summary: Henderson's band is the top band, Paul Whiteman admires it, and Henderson inspects the men each night.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Well, Duke came to town. And he was playing at the Kentucky Club, 48th Street and Broadway. Now, you know, in those days, it wasn't so many musicians, and Fletcher's band was the top band. And Paul Whitman had been named just a couple of years ago the King of Jazz. He was a violinist. And Paul Whitman came himself to hear Fletcher's band, and he said, if Fletcher was a white man, he would be a millionaire. That's just what he said. I heard him.
Well, Fletcher went up and up and up and up and up.

But he was a very strict leader. Every night, you had to stand up and stand inspection. He'd look at your hair, your face, see if you shaved, your shoes, see if they're shined. You had to be perfect to suit him. Of course, poor Louis, he was just the opposite when he joined the band, but all his faults and everything, his deficiencies, he made up in his playing. That -- nobody else could beat him playing at that time.
